findings.title: Excess shard-aware connection dropped without decrementing total_connections
findings.claim: In the requested_shard branch of handle_ready_connection, the connection is dropped after start_opening_connection(None) but total_connections was already incremented by count_in_metrics and nothing decrements it, causing the gauge to drift upward on every excess shard-aware event (e.g. NAT/shard-mismatch).

findings.title: Connections held in conns/excess_connections at run() exit dropped without…
findings.claim: When PoolRefiller::run returns (keyspace channel dropped, node removed), connections still held in conns/excess_connections are dropped and the total_connections gauge is not decremented.

findings.title: Keyspace check now precedes sharder/shard-aware-port update, blocking them on persistent…
findings.claim: With the keyspace check ahead of maybe_reshard and the shard-aware-port update, a node whose USE keeps failing never updates the pool's sharder or shard-aware port, and the pool does not refill until the keyspace exists again; this is a behavior change from silently accepting the connection and should be confirmed as intended.

findings.title: use_keyspace on a new connection has no timeout
findings.claim: start_setting_keyspace_for_connection still carries a TODO that there should be a timeout; a hung USE keeps is_filling() true and stalls refills for that pool.

findings.title: Test re-implements simulated-node proxy setup instead of reusing a shared helper
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state hand-builds the OPTIONS/STARTUP forged-response rules and proxy in a ~60-line make_rules closure, duplicating start_simulated_node and inline rule blocks in the resharding test, making any handshake change require edits in multiple places.

findings.title: Non-empty-pool keyspace-failure test omits refill-flag and requested_shard assertions
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state never asserts had_error_since_last_refill or need_filling(), and no non-empty-pool test feeds requested_shard: Some(..) into that arm to confirm no immediate non-shard-aware retry is scheduled, unlike the Connection error arm.

findings.title: Keyspace failure arm never driven through run() loop to observe backoff-delayed refill
findings.claim: The Keyspace failure arm is exercised only with a forged server error and a synthetic RequestTimeout event; no test drives a failing USE through the run() loop to confirm the backoff-delayed refill actually occurs end to end.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops N atomic decrements
findings.claim: A maintainability note observed that decrement_total_connections loops N atomic decrements, self-described as low impact with no worthwhile benefit to changing it.
